newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Eastern Oil sees higher 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Eastern Oil sees higher 1996 profit.

text.p: Russia's Eastern Oil Co (VNK) expects net profit to have risen to 898.0 billion roubles in 1996 from 722.8 billion in 1995, according to preliminary figures, the company said on Thursday.
Oil production at OAO Vostochnaya Neftyanaya Kompaniya (VNK -- Eastern Oil) was steady at 11.2 million tonnes, Tamara Demesheva, head of Eastern Oil's press service, told Reuters.
The company plans to pay an annual dividend of 3.20 roubles per share with face value of two roubles for 1996, after paying no dividend for 1995, she said.
Eastern Oil is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years. Its main operating unit is Tomskneft.
The federal government owns 51 percent of Eastern Oil, and 15 percent were sold in December 1995.

The government plans to sell 34 percent later this year in an investment tender, but first must issue a resolution approving a decision by shareholders in November last year to remove two oil marketing companies from the group.
